1 Project Overview

This project develops an R-based forecasting analysis using a time series data set obtained from the TÜİK Data Portal. The selected data set is Number of Trips and Overnights of Domestic Visitors by Quarter, under the Tourism theme. The selected variable is Number of Trips.

The purpose of the analysis is to compare alternative forecasting methods and forecast the next unpublished period after the latest available TÜİK observation.

2 Data Source and TÜİK Connection

The data are accessed directly from TÜİK through R. The table is first located using the tuikr package. Since the selected table is an istab table and does not have a TR,DF_... dataflow ID, the official TÜİK table_url returned by tuikr::statistical_tables(theme = "14") is used within R.

data_import <- import_domestic_tourism_data()
selected_table <- data_import$selected_table
data_access_date <- data_import$data_access_date
domestic_data <- data_import$data

3 Use of TÜİK Data in R

The data were not manually downloaded, copied, pasted, edited, or stored as a separate input data file. The workflow is fully reproducible inside R:

  1. The table list is obtained with tuikr::statistical_tables(theme = "14").
  2. The table named Number of Trips and Overnights of Domestic Visitors by Quarter is selected.
  3. The official TÜİK table_url is requested with httr::GET() inside R.
  4. The returned Excel content is read with readxl::read_excel().
  5. Quarterly rows are selected and formatted into a time series using reproducible R code.

4 Exploratory Time Series Analysis

ts_trips <- ts(domestic_data$Trips, start = c(min(domestic_data$Year), 1), frequency = 4)

actual_plot <- ggplot(domestic_data, aes(x = Time_Index, y = Trips)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = domestic_data$Time_Index[seq(1, nrow(domestic_data), by = 4)],
    labels = domestic_data$Period[seq(1, nrow(domestic_data), by = 4)]
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Actual Series: Domestic Visitors' Number of Trips",
    x = "Period",
    y = "Number of trips"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

actual_plot

ggsave("outputs/figures/actual_series_plot.png", actual_plot, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300)

The series is quarterly and exhibits a recurring seasonal pattern across quarters. The third quarter generally records higher values, reflecting the seasonal nature of domestic tourism activity in Türkiye. The series also shows structural variation during the pandemic period, which may influence forecasting performance.

5 Forecasting Methods

forecast_results <- run_forecasting_methods(domestic_data)
model_data <- forecast_results$data_with_fits
next_forecasts <- forecast_results$next_forecasts
target_period <- forecast_results$target_period

5.1 Naïve Forecasting

Naïve forecasting uses the previous period’s actual value as the forecast for the current period.

next_forecasts %>% filter(Method == "Naive Forecasting") %>% kable()
Method Next_Period_Forecast
Naive Forecasting 11022.8 
save_actual_forecast_plot(
  model_data %>% transmute(Time_Index, Period, Actual = Trips, Forecast = Naive),
  "Actual vs Naive Forecast",
  "outputs/figures/naive_forecast_plot.png"
)

5.2 Moving Average

A four-quarter moving average is used because the data are quarterly and one full seasonal cycle contains four quarters.

next_forecasts %>% filter(Method == "Moving Average") %>% kable()
Method Next_Period_Forecast
Moving Average 16962.67 
save_actual_forecast_plot(
  model_data %>% transmute(Time_Index, Period, Actual = Trips, Forecast = Moving_Average),
  "Actual vs Moving Average Forecast",
  "outputs/figures/moving_average_plot.png"
)

5.3 Weighted Moving Average

The weighted moving average gives more importance to recent observations. The weights are 0.40, 0.30, 0.20, and 0.10 for the most recent four quarters.

7 Forecast Accuracy Comparison

The comparison includes Bias, MAD, MSE, MAPE, RSFE, and Tracking Signal. Forecast error is defined as actual minus forecast.

method_columns <- c(
  "Naive Forecasting" = "Naive",
  "Moving Average" = "Moving_Average",
  "Weighted Moving Average" = "Weighted_Moving_Average",
  "Exponential Smoothing" = "Exponential_Smoothing",
  "Trend-Adjusted Exponential Smoothing" = "Trend_Adjusted_Exponential_Smoothing",
  "Linear Trend Projection" = "Linear_Trend_Projection",
  "Seasonal Indices" = "Seasonal_Indices",
  "Additive Decomposition" = "Additive_Decomposition",
  "Multiplicative Decomposition" = "Multiplicative_Decomposition",
  "Regression with Trend and Seasonal Dummies" = "Regression_Trend_Seasonal_Dummies"
)

accuracy_table <- lapply(names(method_columns), function(method_name) {
  forecast_col <- method_columns[[method_name]]
  metrics <- accuracy_measures(model_data$Trips, model_data[[forecast_col]])
  next_value <- next_forecasts$Next_Period_Forecast[next_forecasts$Method == method_name]
  data.frame(Method = method_name, metrics, Next_Period_Forecast = next_value)
}) %>% bind_rows()

write.csv(accuracy_table, "outputs/tables/accuracy_comparison.csv", row.names = FALSE)

8 Superior Method Selection

The superior method is selected primarily based on MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error), while also considering the suitability of the method for a quarterly seasonal time series. Among the evaluated methods, Additive Decomposition achieved the lowest MAPE and was therefore selected as the superior forecasting method. Tracking Signal is also considered as a monitoring measure for systematic bias.

applicable_methods <- accuracy_table %>%
  filter(is.finite(MAPE), is.finite(Tracking_Signal)) %>%
  mutate(abs_tracking_signal = abs(Tracking_Signal))

superior <- applicable_methods %>%
  arrange(MAPE, abs_tracking_signal) %>%
  slice(1)

superior %>% kable(digits = 2)
Method Bias MAD MSE MAPE RSFE Tracking_Signal Next_Period_Forecast abs_tracking_signal
Additive Decomposition 12.7 1430 3432818 9.49 813.07 0.57 11602.61 0.57

The selected method is superior for this TÜİK time series because it performs well in the numerical accuracy comparison and is appropriate for the observed quarterly structure of the data.

9 Final Next-Period Forecast

final_forecast <- data.frame(
  Selected_Superior_Method = superior$Method,
  Data_Access_Date = as.character(data_access_date),
  Latest_Available_Observation = domestic_data$Period[nrow(domestic_data)],
  Forecast_Target_Period = target_period,
  Forecasted_Value = superior$Next_Period_Forecast,
  MAPE = superior$MAPE,
  MAD = superior$MAD,
  MSE = superior$MSE,
  Tracking_Signal = superior$Tracking_Signal
)

write.csv(final_forecast, "outputs/tables/final_forecast.csv", row.names = FALSE)
final_forecast %>% kable(digits = 2)
Selected_Superior_Method Data_Access_Date Latest_Available_Observation Forecast_Target_Period Forecasted_Value MAPE MAD MSE Tracking_Signal
Additive Decomposition 2026-05-31 2025 Q4 2026 Q1 11602.61 9.49 1430 3432818 0.57 
superior_col <- method_columns[[superior$Method]]
future_point <- data.frame(
  Time_Index = max(model_data$Time_Index) + 1,
  Period = target_period,
  Actual = NA_real_,
  Forecast = superior$Next_Period_Forecast
)

superior_plot_data <- bind_rows(
  model_data %>% transmute(Time_Index, Period, Actual = Trips, Forecast = .data[[superior_col]]),
  future_point
)

p_superior <- ggplot(superior_plot_data, aes(x = Time_Index)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Actual, linetype = "Actual"), linewidth = 0.8, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Forecast, linetype = "Fitted/Forecast"), linewidth = 0.8, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(data = future_point, aes(y = Forecast), size = 3, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = superior_plot_data$Time_Index[seq(1, nrow(superior_plot_data), by = 4)],
    labels = superior_plot_data$Period[seq(1, nrow(superior_plot_data), by = 4)]
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title = paste("Superior Method and", target_period, "Forecast"), x = "Period", y = "Number of trips", linetype = "Series") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

p_superior

10 Interpretation of Results

The final forecast estimates the number of domestic tourism trips for the next unpublished quarterly period. The result should be interpreted as a quantitative forecast based only on the historical TÜİK time series. It does not include explanatory variables such as household income, inflation, transport costs, holidays, exchange rates, or policy changes.

11 Limitations

The main limitations are:

  • The models use only past values of the selected TÜİK series.
  • Future shocks, policy changes, holidays, macroeconomic conditions, and tourism behavior changes are not explicitly modeled.
  • The pandemic period creates a structural break that may affect forecast accuracy.
  • Tracking Signal values should be interpreted carefully because systematic bias may appear after large shocks or sharp seasonal changes.
  • TÜİK data may be revised in later releases.

12 Reproducibility Notes

To reproduce the project:

  1. Install the required R packages listed in the setup chunk.
  2. Open forecasting_project.Rmd.
  3. Knit the file to HTML.
  4. The notebook will access the TÜİK table through tuikr::statistical_tables(theme = "14"), download the official TÜİK table URL inside R, clean the data, run the forecasting methods, and generate output tables and figures.

No manually downloaded or manually edited data file is required.
